July 3, 1971
scheme E shows a smaller cul-de-sac located immediately northwest of the school building. This cul-de-sac would be used primarily as a turnaround for the residents of Sunnyside Street. This scheme take 675 square feet from the area north of the school and 3,530 square feet from the playground west of the school. The closing of Sunnyside Street provides an additional 7,740 of playground space. For this scheme the gain in playground area is 3,535 square feet and the not loss of school property is 1,725 square feet.
Scheme C is accomplished by widening the alley north of the playground area between Sunnyside and Franklin Streets. For this situation, 3,530 square feet are taken from both the north and south sides of the playground area. An increase of 7,380 square feet is provided by the closing of Sunnyside Street and the gain in playground area is 320 square feet. The resultant overall loss of school property is 4,940 square feet.
Scheme D provides a cul-de-sac on Sunnyside Street north of the school building by taking of 650 square feet from a privately-owned vacant lot adjacent to the alley north of the play area. The taking from the playground area west of the school is 3,530 square feet, but by closing a portion of Sunnyside Street, 8,100 square feet are added to the playground area. This yields a gain of 4,570 square feet for playground space, but a net loss of 690 square feet of school property.
Ly closing a percion of Sunnyside Street the present playground area to the west of the school becomes immediately contiguous to the school building, thus eliminating the hazard inherent in school children crossing the street to use the facility. The present main access point for the pickup or dropoff of students is on Sunnyside Street. Under the proposed schemes, this function could readily be transferred to the Prairie Street entrance. Fire apparatus can most conveniently reach the school building by entering the paved area east and north of the building from Prairie Street. This access is unaffected by the proposed schemes.
A response from your City at an early date to the above proposals would be very beneficial to our study. If you require additional information on this matter or have questions, please do not hesitate to contact this office.
Very truly yours,
Sigmund C. Ziejewski Regional Transportation Engineer
